content.text: No minimum-commitment or volume-cap mechanic appears anywhere; fees are tied to licences granted, services ordered, and actual revenue.

input.quote: 4.1 License Fees. In consideration for the licenses granted to Corio pursuant to Section 2 of this Agreement, Corio shall pay the license fees specified in EXHIBIT B hereto.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no minimum purchase or volume commitment on Corio and no take-or-pay, shortfall-penalty or usage-cap mechanic. Corio's payment obligations are consideration for what it actually licenses and orders: the one-time BuySite licence fee due on Software Acceptance (§4.1, Exhibit B Payment Terms), the annual MarketSite.net access fee for the access it takes (§2.6, Exhibit B), the annual maintenance and support fee for support services (§4.2, which continues "provided that Corio continues to pay"), implementation fees on a time-and-materials basis capped at a maximum, and a percentage revenue share calculated on actual Application Management Revenue from live Corio Customers. Volume terms run in our favour rather than against us: Software Users are "Unlimited" and Corio may sublicense "an unlimited number of Customers". The only use of "minimum" affecting fees (Exhibit B §2.A, the 40-Authorized-User limitation) is a condition on a revenue-share exemption that benefits Corio, not a committed volume, and the "shortfall" reference in §4.4 is an audit true-up payable by whichever party underpaid. This sits at the preferred position, so no redline is warranted. We note only that the five-year initial term (§11.1) is terminable by Corio for breach or insolvency rather than at will; that is a term-length/exit point under the termination rules, not a minimum-commitment issue, and we do not flag it twice here.
